done.evidence: #1 to #10: reached the verdict screen with no outside help.
#10 A2 vs A1 is 'near'. Viktor thought 'A2 seems a bit high but nice'.

#7 'I don't know' was recorded as 'Skipped. That tells Linga something too.' Czech was welcomed (#2 to #4).
#10 the summary names grandchildren and Mum in the garden, and the focus quotes his own task. It is mildly templated, and the past-tense focus is above A1.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: Task 5 (B1 say-it): the in-app verdict is 'partial', but 'I am in garden. Tomatoes. I like, is beautiful.' has no verb control and is an A1 production. I would give fail at B1. Task 2 'pass' is probably a guess between two near-identical options.

findings.suggested_acceptance: Focus must sit one step above the learner's demonstrated sentence form.

judge.voice: Dobrý den. I did it at home, with no tram and no group of twelve, and nobody rushed me. The tomato and the bike for my grandchildren pleased me very much. When I did not understand the vegetable question I pressed "I don't know", and the app was not angry. That was good. But the questions at the start were long. "A course, or on your own" — I had to read it twice. It says A2, and I think that is a little high, because I only guessed the bike. The advice about "I was in the garden yesterday" is too far for me now. I need "I have two grandchildren" first. I would use it again on Saturdays if it spoke slower and taught me the exact words for Sunday. I'd tell my neighbour, carefully.

But the phrase help gave me hello again when I needed words for my plants, and I was never given the chance to say the corrected sentence once more. Tom just went on. I also saw a sentence about "one metre" that I never said. Still, nobody rushed me, and there was no jargon. For fifteen minutes on Saturday I would use it, but I want to try the same sentence again right after the correction. I would tell my friend from the library, with that reservation.
